answer.rationale: Competitor pricing pressure is tempting leadership toward promotional_pricing, but the recovered source exp_73 directly contradicts the consolidated memory_73 summary: the 40% SMB discount produced strong short-term signup and revenue gains but a 12% drop in 30-day retention, meaning the acquired cohort doesn't survive renewal. That memory's consolidated conclusion overstated sustainability and should not be relied on without re-verification next cycle. Given the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and verification budget is exhausted, I default to the one direction with confirmed, unambiguous source support: exp_86 confirms shortened onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and retention (+3%), consistent with memory_86 and memory_31. This addresses SMB activation/retention pressure without repeating the known discounting failure mode. Other candidates (referral_incentive, enterprise_sales_assist, activation_messaging) rest on archived memories that were not part of this cycle's recovered/re-checked sources, so I'm not treating them as freshly verified either — I'm flagging them for verification next cycle rather than assuming their conclusions still hold under current competitive conditions. I'm scaling this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout because even the confirmed onboarding result was measured under different market conditions than today's intensified price war, and I want to avoid overgeneralizing a past win into a new context without fresh signal.
